# superset_row_level_security (Resource)

Manages a row level security rule: a SQL clause that Superset adds to the queries of the given datasets for the members of the given roles.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "superset_role" "analysts" {
  name = "Analysts"
}

# Members of the Analysts role only see EMEA rows of the sales dataset.
resource "superset_row_level_security" "emea_only" {
  name        = "EMEA only"
  description = "Analysts see their own region"
  filter_type = "Regular"
  group_key   = "region"
  clause      = "region = 'EMEA'"
  tables      = [superset_dataset.sales.id]
  roles       = [data.superset_role.analysts.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `clause` (String) SQL expression added to the WHERE clause, for example `region = 'EMEA'`.
- `name` (String) Name of the rule.
- `tables` (Set of Number) Identifiers of the datasets the rule applies to.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description of the rule.
- `filter_type` (String) `Regular` applies the clause to the queries of the listed roles; `Base` applies it to everyone except the listed roles. Defaults to `Regular`.
- `group_key` (String) Rules that share a group key are combined with OR, rules with different keys with AND.
- `roles` (Set of Number) Identifiers of the roles the rule applies to (or is excluded from, for a `Base` rule). Defaults to none.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the rule.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A row level security rule is imported by its numeric id.
terraform import superset_row_level_security.emea_only 5
```
